_comment: An image overlay that reveals over a treated copy of the film -- the end-card grammar. Modelled on the Invest Like the Best end card (x.com/patrick_oshag/status/1985693514357756286 at 1:26:25), read frame by frame at 6fps: over about 1.5s the wide shot desaturates to black and white, blurs and darkens while it KEEPS PLAYING, and the show logo -- a PNG with real alpha -- reveals left to right behind a hard edge, then holds to the end. Everything below is that reading, generalised: the treatment is opt-in per overlay, so a mid-video logo does not dim the film by surprise.

layout._note: corner is top/bottom x left/right, or anything else for centred -- the same vocabulary as the name label. width_frac sizes the image as a fraction of the frame width, which is how a card stays the same size on a 1080p film and a 1080x1920 short.

animation._note: in.type is wipe / fade / slide / none. feather_px softens the wipe's leading edge -- the reference is hard, so keep it small; a soft edge suits photographic images. direction is left/right/up/down: for a wipe it is the edge the reveal starts FROM, for a slide the edge the image travels in from.

background._note: Applied to the film under the image while the overlay is up, and only if the overlay asks for it. desaturate 1.0 is fully black and white; dim is how much brightness is subtracted; blur_sigma is a gaussian on the whole frame. in_s/out_s are the ramps -- the treated layer is cross-faded over the sharp one, which reads as a progressive blur without needing sendcmd.

html_render._note: Defaults for a Claude-authored card rendered by html-to-image.py. Named html_render rather than html because on an overlay entry `html` is the page's path -- one name for two shapes would be merged with a string and explode. viewport is the browser window; the shot is cropped to its own alpha afterwards, so make the window comfortably bigger than the artwork. device_scale 2 keeps type crisp when the card is scaled onto a 1080p frame.

_measured._note: The reference staggers the wipe per line of the logo, which this preset does not do yet -- a single-image wipe is one expression, a staggered one is the same expression with floor(Y/line_h)*delay added to the progress term. Reserved as animation.in.stagger.
